title: On Urging the boys on through the rain
subtitle: 责任担当 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）
meta: 主题语境：责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）　|　核心词汇：urge　|　正文 358 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 urge 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the fisherman ① urged the boys on through the rain on the same day, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② urges the boys on through the rain before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ urge the boys on through the rain at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ urged the boys on through the rain before — a line in the logbook for July 1987 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Urging the boys on through the rain on the same day, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ urge everybody to wait one day before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Urge everybody to wait one day at once and never mention it again.

By 2000 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ urges everybody to wait one day on the same day every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ urged the boys on through the rain again when nobody else would.

⑩ To urge the boys on through the rain, my mother said in 2005, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody urges the boys on through the rain before dawn again and somebody must urge the boys on through the rain on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 催促（一般过去式 urged the boys on through the rain：1993 年渔人头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 催促（一般现在 urges the boys on through the rain：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 催促（不定式 to urge the boys on through the rain：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 催促（过去完成时 had urged the boys on through the rain：1987 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 催促（动名词 urging the boys on through the rain 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 力劝（urge everybody to wait one day：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去力劝力劝大家再等一天）
G. v. 力劝（urge everybody to wait one day：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 催促（后段两处：新来的船工照例 urges everybody to wait one day，而母亲又一次 urged the boys on through the rain）

answers.why: urge 意为“催促”，1993 年渔人当天就催促催着孩子们冒雨前进，那是渔港里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 urged。
urge 意为“催促”，自那以后渔人天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 urges。
urge 意为“催促”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯催促催着孩子们冒雨前进”，此处为不定式 to urge the boys on through the rain。
urge 意为“催促”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 2000 年之前就有人催促过，故用过去完成时 had urged。
urge 意为“催促”，渔人说“催促催着孩子们冒雨前进这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 urging the boys on through the rain 作主语。
urge 意为“力劝”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去力劝力劝大家再等一天”，should ever 之后用原形 urge everybody to wait one day。
urge 意为“力劝”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻力劝力劝大家再等一天（urge everybody to wait one day at once），以后再也不要提起。
urge 意为“催促”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例力劝力劝大家再等一天，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 urges。
urge 意为“催促”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就催促催着孩子们冒雨前进，用一般过去式 urged 叙述。
urge 意为“催促”，结尾那句是母亲 2005 年的话：要催促催着孩子们冒雨前进，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 urge 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1993 the fisherman urged the boys on through the rain on the same day, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman urges the boys on through the rain before dawn whenever the harbour asks.
Urging the boys on through the rain on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever urge everybody to wait one day before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour urges everybody to wait one day on the same day every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother urged the boys on through the rain again, and the harbour remembered that half.
